hazard_consequence_node.label: HazardConsequence
hazard_consequence_node.name: Confined explosion
hazard_consequence_node.evidence: "the initial explosion occurred inside a vertical above-ground storage tank that was being filled with VM&P naphtha."
hazard_consequence_node.explanation: The incident analysis is centered on an internal tank explosion during filling. The report mainly examines how an ignitable vapor-air mixture formed in the tank headspace and how static accumulation and a likely spark from the gauging float linkage ignited it. The later fireball, tank ruptures, and tank farm fire were escalation effects following the primary internal explosion.

entity_nodes.label: Material
entity_nodes.name: VM&P naphtha
entity_nodes.explanation: VM&P naphtha was the flammable liquid being transferred into the tank and generated the ignitable headspace vapor-air mixture involved in the explosion.

entity_nodes.label: Location
entity_nodes.name: 15,000 gallon above-ground storage tank
entity_nodes.evidence: into a 15,000 gallon above-ground storage tank
entity_nodes.explanation: The initial explosion occurred in the storage tank that was receiving the final compartment of the tanker-trailer.

condition_nodes.label: Phase
condition_nodes.name: Vapor
condition_nodes.evidence: The tank contained an ignitable vapor-air mixture in its head space.
condition_nodes.explanation: The confined explosion involved the vapor phase in the tank headspace.

condition_nodes.label: Temperature
condition_nodes.name: Atmospheric temperature
condition_nodes.evidence: at approximately 77˚F (25˚C) (the handling temperature of the VM&P naphtha at the time of the incident)
condition_nodes.explanation: The material was handled at ambient conditions when the ignitable vapor-air mixture was present.

condition_nodes.label: Volatility
condition_nodes.name: High volatility
condition_nodes.evidence: can produce ignitable vapor-air mixtures inside tanks
condition_nodes.explanation: The material readily generated ignitable vapors in the tank at the incident temperature.

condition_nodes.label: Combustibility
condition_nodes.name: Combustible
condition_nodes.evidence: VM&P naphtha is a National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) Class IB flammable liquid
condition_nodes.explanation: The substance was a flammable liquid capable of burning and exploding when mixed with air and ignited.

condition_nodes.label: Conductivity
condition_nodes.name: Low conductivity
condition_nodes.evidence: because of its low electrical conductivity, can accumulate dangerous levels of static electricity.
condition_nodes.explanation: Low conductivity allowed static charge to accumulate during transfer operations.

condition_nodes.label: Confinement
condition_nodes.name: High confinement
condition_nodes.evidence: the initial explosion occurred inside a vertical above-ground storage tank
condition_nodes.explanation: The flammable vapor-air mixture was enclosed within the storage tank, creating a highly confined explosion environment.

event_nodes.label: InitiatingEvent
event_nodes.name: Rapid static charge accumulation during stop-start filling
event_nodes.evidence: Stop-start filling, air in the transfer piping, and sediment and water (likely present in the tank) caused a rapid static charge accumulation inside the VM&P naphtha tank.
event_nodes.explanation: This was the earliest abnormal process condition identified as initiating the sequence that led to ignition of the headspace vapor-air mixture.

event_nodes.label: MechanicalFailure
event_nodes.name: Gauge float linkage likely separated during filling
event_nodes.evidence: "turbulence and bubbling during the stop-start transfer pumping, in addition to creating rapid static charge accumulation, also likely created slack in the gauge tape connected to the float, causing the linkage to separate"
event_nodes.explanation: The explanation should emphasize that Ev2 represents the actual linkage separation during filling; the loose-linkage design is the latent feature that made that separation possible.

event_nodes.label: IgnitionSource
event_nodes.name: Spark from separated gauging float linkage
event_nodes.evidence: The tank had a liquid level gauging system float with a loose linkage that likely separated and created a spark during filling.
event_nodes.explanation: The likely ignition source was a spark generated by the gauging float linkage during filling, which ignited the headspace vapor-air mixture.

event_nodes.label: InitiatingEvent
event_nodes.name: Turbulence and bubbling during stop-start transfer pumping
event_nodes.evidence: The report states that "turbulence and bubbling during the stop-start transfer pumping, in addition to creating rapid static charge accumulation, also likely created slack in the gauge tape connected to the float, causing the linkage to separate and spark."
event_nodes.explanation: The report describes stop-start transfer turbulence/bubbling as the shared operational precursor that contributed both to rapid static accumulation and to slack/separation in the gauging linkage. Adding this node makes the causal chain more explicit without changing the main scenario.
